accepts.because: a screened turn on its way to the surface -- the one a channel of the MEMBER raised and the member's firewall passed back down. Since GH #454 the channel is one level up: it belongs to the person, not to one of their generations, so a second assistant of the same person is reached through the same bot by name. The turn arrives with `context.channel_node` (the node the answer routes back to), `context.channel` (the chat it is in -- GH #522), `context.user_id` and `context.audience_set` already stamped by the channel's own edge and re-stamped by the member's door, and with `context.assistant` naming which of the person's agents it was addressed to -- the member's container reads that key and nothing below it does. Derived from the accepts list of talky@5.0.0, which is what stands in ./talky

a memory bundle, coming back from whatever keeps this person's memory -- under GH #122 that is the MEMBER's memory hive, one level up, because two assistants of one person must know the same person. Since GH #562 this level does not CARRY the bundle down, it VOUCHES for where it lands: the lane is a v-lane (ADR-0020), the connect points are the two askers, and the edge that delivers is drawn once, in the container this generation stands in. What used to be two hops -- a door here plus a door in the container -- is one, and the two doors that told the askers apart moved with it unchanged: `hop.recall_caller == 'cogny'` reaches the reasoning core, anything else -- including nothing at all -- takes the DEFAULT edge to ./talky, which is where every bundle went before. The token is the asker's own, stamped on the way out and handed back onto the hop by the memory hive itself (memory-hive `bundle`); this level mints none of it and reads nothing else in it. Derived from the accepts list of talky@5.0.0

an advisor's answer arriving as its own turn. The reasoning core inside this level answers on this lane too (./cogny -> ./talky), and the lane stays outward-facing for the other case: a SECOND agent, outside this assistant, that was asked something and answered late. Derived from the accepts list of talky@5.0.0

an operator-forced session sweep outside the night timer. It belongs to whoever operates the colony, not to anything inside this level, which is why it enters at the assistant path rather than being produced by a sibling. Derived from the accepts list of talky@5.0.0

a prune verdict for the context window, from a timer or an operator. It is paired with the `prune` report in `params.required_drains`: a prune answers unconditionally, and an operator who sends one without taking the report back cuts unwitnessed. Derived from the accepts list of talky@5.0.0

a round that ran out of iterations, swept by an operator. Same owner as `in_sweep` and the same reason it crosses the level boundary rather than starting inside it. Derived from the accepts list of talky@5.0.0

the builder's answer on its way back to the tool round that asked -- a draft manifest, or the receipt of one that was submitted. It enters at the assistant path because its producer sits four levels up, at the OS level, where a level owns what its siblings must share (ADR-0013): one baumeister, one corpus, one audit trail for every organisation in the colony. This level only carries it down to the tool surface; it reads nothing in it. Derived from the accepts list of tools@1.4.1

a durable `system.*` slot for this generation's brains -- `identity`, `persona`, `handover` or `instructions`, and nothing else. The charter is on that list since GH #488: it had been held out of the lane to keep a subscription from overwriting what the agent is for, which assumed it had another owner, and it had none -- so a rebuilt generation came up with an empty charter and answered as the vendor's default assistant. SINCE GH #561 THIS LEVEL DOES NOT CARRY THE LANE -- IT VOUCHES FOR IT. `at` names the two rims a v-lane on `in_pack` may end at, which is the whole of what this level has to say about the pack: the sender draws ONE edge per rim straight from its own `affinity` to `./talky` and `./cogny` (GH #559), and the two hops that used to stand in between are gone. A level that declared the lane and only forwarded it claimed an influence it never took -- it stamped nothing, filtered nothing, guarded nothing -- so what is left here is the permission and the address, and `ports: []` at each rim stays literally true because the exception is pronounced by the target and never taken by the caller. The fan-out is still a fan-out and still for the same reason: the surface's brain and the core's brain are the same agent, and a generation whose channel voice knew who it was while its reasoning core did not would answer as two different people. It is now two EDGES the sender draws rather than two edges this level draws, and the pack is still written once per `llm` cell behind each rim -- each upserts into its own `cell.db`, which is the only place durable system state can live. WHAT THE FAN-OUT COSTS THE AUTHOR, measured on a live generation (GH #538): one text reaches two occupants with different MENUS, so an instruction that obliges the reader to call a tool has to say which reader it is for. A charter sharpened into *`consult_cogny` is mandatory* made the CORE -- which does not carry that name, because it IS the core -- answer three consultations in a row with `the reasoning core is not available in this session`. The cure is a role test inside the sentence (`if consult_cogny is on your menu`) plus the other half said out loud (`if it is not, you are the core`), not a second pack: this lane is deliberately one document for one agent. Derived from the accepts lists of talky@5.0.0 and cogny@5.0.0 (GH #458). PAIRED with `pack_ack` in `params.required_drains`

a demand that this generation hand out the one store it holds that the member cannot recompute: the session ledger of `./talky`, which decides whether a conversation continues or starts at zero. The lane crosses this level unchanged into the surface, which passes it on to its own keeper (talky@5.0.0 -> session-keeper@2.1.0, GH #475). Neither this level nor the surface reads a part or decides what may leave -- that is the keeper's own walk, the same arrangement the member's three holders have had since GH #471. Since GH #555 the keeper's own STORE writes the ledger, so what leaves here is the completion word `export_done` and, on the way back in, the receipt of an applied part on `dump`; the member carries both out

one part of such a document, for a generation that is already running. The other half of `in_export` and the return leg of the same document: the keeper's seed was read once, when its `cell.db` was created, so a ledger walked out of another colony after that moment has no way in except a message. It crosses unchanged into `./talky` (talky@5.0.0). WHICH generation a part belongs to is decided one level up, in the member's own container, by the edge that addresses this assistant -- a member with two generations has two ledgers, and they are not one document (GH #475)

the answer to a `memory_recall` call this generation made, coming back off the member's own memory (GH #552). It arrives at the level and not at the asker, because the level is what knows which of its two occupants asked: `context.tool_caller` was stamped on the way out and the two entry edges read it. The same restamping the tools hive's results already get one storey down, one storey up Derived from the accepts lists of talky@5.0.0 and cogny@5.0.0 (GH #552).

the memory's own declaration of that tool, on its way to whichever occupant asked (GH #552). It carries `context.tool_answerer == 'memory'`, which is what lets the asking collector MERGE a third answerer's declarations into its menu instead of overwriting them (GH #529) Derived from the accepts lists of talky@5.0.0 and cogny@5.0.0 (GH #552).

the mutation receipt, GH #553: the graph moved, and the door said so. It enters at the hive `colony.json` names in `mutation_receipts.to` and is drawn onwards ONE LEVEL AT A TIME -- this level declares it and routes it into `./talky` and `./cogny`, which is what makes it a mandatory hop under ADR-0020: nothing may carry this lane past a level that takes part in it. It replaces a poll: the tool menu of a generation used to ask a timer's question every five minutes, and the boot receipt is the first fill, so a colony that has just started already knows. Derived from talky@5.0.0 and cogny@5.0.0

emits.because: what this generation said, on its way back to the channel that asked. It is the lane GH #454 added and the mirror of what it removed: `turn` used to leave here because the channel was INSIDE the assistant and its raw wire had to reach the member's screen from within. The channel is now the member's, so the raw turn never enters this level at all -- what enters is a screened turn and what leaves is the answer to it. The assistant does not know which channel it came from and must not: `context.channel_node` rode in on the turn and rides back out on the answer, and the member's own edge into ./channels is what turns that name into an address. Derived from the emits list of talky@5.0.0, where it was consumed one level down by a connector standing beside the surface -- the connector moved out, so the lane crosses

a closed session as one write batch, for wherever a day belongs. It carries `context.channel` and `context.audience_set` off the generation row rather than off the sweep that ended it. The assistant does not consume it -- no store of any kind lives at this level. Derived from the emits list of talky@5.0.0

ONE finished turn per message, after every stored turn and every stored answer -- never a batch (GH #298, ruling Q11). It is the shape a memory hive's episode lane reads, and that hive belongs to the member (GH #122). Derived from the emits list of talky@5.0.0

the sidecar a turn's answer carried, in the inline contract form, one message per annotated turn and never repaired. It routes UPWARD to the member's memory hive `in_remember` door, exactly where talky's own shipped recipe sends it (templates/talky/README.md, 'two edges, never one'), because under GH #122 the memory belongs to the member. The assistant grows no memory of its own: a second store would force the writer to pick a store before extraction has run. Derived from the emits list of talky@5.0.0

a memory read this turn needs, for the member's memory hive. ONE lane, TWO askers since GH #532: the conversation surface and the reasoning core. Since GH #562 they leave on a v-lane rather than through this rim (ADR-0020): the `at` list is this level saying which of its occupants the lane docks on, and it is the whole of what it says about the lane -- it does not stamp, filter or guard it, and a level that only forwards a lane has no business being a hop. The member one level up is the opposite case and stays in the road: it declares the same lane, names no connect point for an asker, and turns `recall` into `in_query` with the audience, the room and the as-of on it. Each asker stamps `context.recall_caller` with its own name on the way out -- 'talky' or 'cogny' -- on the v-lane the container draws. That token is the whole of what identifies the asker, and it travels in CONTEXT because nothing else survives the hive (GH #411); the hive hands it back on the hop of the returning `in_bundle`, which is the compartment a door of this level is allowed to be guarded on. STAMPED, never defaulted: the core's answer re-enters the surface on `in_advice` carrying the core's whole context, so a leg that only wrote the token when it was missing would inherit 'cogny' from the consultation it just had and post its own bundle through the core's door. A caller at this boundary sends nothing new -- the lane is the same lane, and the second asker costs it no key. Derived from the emits list of talky@5.0.0 and of the reasoning core in ./cogny

the report of a window prune: one message per cut session, or a single zero report saying nothing was eligible. Paired with `in_prune` in `params.required_drains`. Derived from the emits list of talky@5.0.0

a normalised failure report from anything inside this generation -- the surface or the reasoning core. A CHANNEL's failure is no longer among them: since GH #454 the connector stands in the member's `channels` container and its failures leave on the member's own `error` lane, one level up and beside this one. Which cell produced it is not the caller's business; the assistant is a boundary, not a consumer, and an error that crosses it is one the parent owes a drain. Derived from the emits lists of talky@5.0.0 and cogny@5.0.0

a structural wish leaving this generation, or a manifest being submitted by whoever drafted it. It is the one lane on which a tool of this assistant reaches OUT of the assistant, and it is declared rather than hidden: the reach exists, and a contract that did not name it would be the same defect `sandbox_union` was written to fix one level down. Derived from the emits list of tools@1.4.1

the receipt of one pack, unconditionally -- accepted and refused alike. Since GH #561 it rides the road it came in on: the same two rims, the same one edge each, `lane: "pack_ack"`, back out to whoever drew the corridor. `at` is here for the same reason it is on `in_pack` and says the same thing from the other side -- a v-lane is judged at BOTH of its endpoints, so the level that vouches for the push has to vouch for the receipt too, or the way back is refused `v_lane_no_connect_point`. Drawing one without the other is refused anyway, and now at the rim rather than here: talky@5.0.0 and cogny@5.0.0 pair the two lanes in their own `params.required_drains`, and it is their pairing the door reads once the corridor ends at them. TWO receipts travel per pack and that is the lane's arithmetic rather than a defect: the fan-out is to two sealed occupants, each of which answers once for itself (the cogny answers once for both of its brains). A caller therefore counts OCCUPANTS and not packs, and the sender that pushed reads its own delivery off `hop.pack_owner` and `hop.error_code`, both of which every receipt carries. Joining the two into one would need a cell at this level to hold them, and this level holds no state of any kind. Derived from the emits lists of talky@5.0.0 and cogny@5.0.0 (GH #458)

the keeper inside `./talky` has written its session ledger out completely and says so itself (GH #555): `hop.export_hive` names the hive, `hop.seed_dir` the directory relative to the fence its store declares. Carried out of this level unchanged, on the same terms as `dump`. Derived from the emits list of talky@5.0.0

the receipt of one applied import part, raised by the keeper inside `./talky` and carried out of this level unchanged: `hop.rows_written` counts the inserts it dispatched. Since 0.30.0 the lane carries NOTHING ELSE -- an export writes its own files and reports on `export_done` (GH #555). Drain it with a PLAIN `hop.route == 'dump'` edge -- an edge that tests a second key reads as no drain under the required_drains probe. Derived from the emits list of talky@5.0.0

a `memory_recall` call one of this level's two brains made, on its way OUT of the level to the member's memory (GH #552). It is the one tool name that leaves here: everything else this level can answer it answers inside, at `./tools` or at `./cogny`, and the named edge beside the default is what takes this one out. The member is the mandatory hop -- it is the level that knows the round the question is asked in, and a recall without an audience is refused rather than answered unfiltered Derived from the emits lists of talky@5.0.0 and cogny@5.0.0 (GH #552).

the menu tick of an occupant, on its way out to the member's memory (GH #552). Inside the level the same question already reaches `./tools` and `./cogny`; this is the third answerer, and it lives outside because a memory belongs to the MEMBER and not to one of its generations Derived from the emits lists of talky@5.0.0 and cogny@5.0.0 (GH #552).

required_drains.because: a parent that sends turns into an assistant and does not take its failures back has built a generation whose every failure is a dead letter. This pairing was the retired channel hive's own; it moved up here with the lanes in GH #303 and stays here through GH #454. `in_turn -> answer` is deliberately NOT a second pairing: the answer's consumer is a channel of the member, one level up, and an assistant instantiated before its person has a channel is a legitimate intermediate state. The obligation is real but it is the MEMBER's, and member@1.3.0 ships the edge (`./assistants -> ./channels` on `answer`) that discharges it

a prune answers unconditionally -- with what it cut, or with a zero report saying nothing was eligible. Undrained, every operator prune dead-letters its own answer and the deletions run unwitnessed: the cut happened, nobody can say what fell. Taken from talky@4.3.0, which pairs the same two lanes one level down

a pack answers unconditionally -- with the slots it wrote, or with the code that refused it. Undrained, every push dead-letters its own receipt and the sender's `sent_at` stamp records a delivery nobody can confirm. Taken from talky@5.0.0 and cogny@5.0.0, which pair the same two lanes one level down. Since GH #561 it is THEIR pairing that the door actually reads on a drawn corridor -- a v-lane ends at a rim, and the check that obliges the receipt is the one belonging to the hive the edge names. This entry stays because the statement stays true of the level: whoever is given the corridor is given both halves of it, and one drawn without the other is a push whose receipt nobody takes
the export IS this lane -- wired without it, the keeper's store writes its seed set and nobody is ever told where, or that it finished at all. Taken from the level below, which pairs the same two

the receipt of an applied part is the only positive signal an import has -- undrained, nobody ever learns whether a transfer landed. Taken from talky@5.0.0 and session-keeper@2.1.0, which pair the same two lanes one and two levels down

description.purpose: One generation of one person's agent: the conversation surface, the reasoning core and the tool surface. Three refs and no container at all. Since GH #454 the level is complete at birth: the channels moved up to the MEMBER, so what used to be an open `channels` container filled one mutation per channel is now one shipped `talky` -- the talky that keeps this generation's sessions -- wired to its two siblings by edges of this template. A second channel costs nothing here; it is a node in the person's `channels` container and an edge that names this assistant.
description.use_when: One per generation of an assistant, instantiated into a member's ./assistants container, with its transit lanes wired in the same mutation. Nothing comes afterwards: there is no per-channel follow-up mutation any more. Give the generation its model and its prompt with `override_params` on `<assistant>/talky/brain` and `<assistant>/talky/collector`. The member's own container is what decides which generation a turn was addressed to -- one edge per assistant, guarded on `context.assistant`, drawn by the mutation that instantiates this node (templates/member/README.md, 'Addressing an assistant through a channel'). Replacing the generation replaces this node; the older one stays in place, silent and readable.
description.not_in_scope: No channel and no connector: a channel belongs to the PERSON, not to one of their generations (GH #454) -- a bot a generation owned would have to be re-created on every swap, and a screen two agents share could not hang anywhere. No memory hive and no memory-drain: the memory belongs to the MEMBER (GH #122, ADR 0012) and per-turn extraction (GH #298, ruling Q11) replaced the drain -- `extraction` leaves this level on its own lane. No firewall: the screen sits one level up, outside the generation, so two channels meet one view of an attacker and a swap does not restart the rate window. No terminal and no sink of any kind (ruling Q2, GH #284): `error` leaves the level and becomes no_route in the DLQ if nobody consumes it, which is recorded and self-localising. No tool schemas of its own: since GH #464 they live in ./tools, beside the cells they describe, and each caller inside this level ASKS for the ones its own template declares -- the answer lands in the calling brain's system.tools, which is where a menu was always read from and is now no longer typed.
description.contract_derivation: The twenty-five lanes are the union of what this level's three occupants accept and emit at the versions named in each `because` (talky in ./talky, cogny, tools), minus the lanes a sibling inside the level consumes itself. ONE subtraction since GH #552: `tool_call`/`tool_result`, the tool surface's own pair, both ends inside. `tool` and `in_tool` were two more until then and are not any more -- one tool name, `memory_recall`, leaves this level for the member's own memory (a named edge beside the guarded default) and its result comes back, so both lanes cross and are declared; everything else on `tool` is still consumed inside by ./tools. `in_thread_call` is declared by talky and is deliberately NOT declared here: no occupant outside this level produces it, and giving it a door would be an interface promising something nothing sends (GH #55 serves it inside the talky). `in_memory_call` stood beside it until talky@5.0.0 and is gone from the library. Until GH #532 the reasoning core's `recall` was the one occupant emit with no home, and the reason it gave was a real constraint read one step short: at this boundary the surface's recall leg and the core's collapse onto ONE lane pair, a hop key does not survive the member's memory hive (GH #411 -- the `recall` cell forms its own hop, and only context travels), and a door guarded on context ALONE is condemned by crates/meclaw-cells/tests/gh173_shipped_hive_contracts.rs, whose probe carries a bare route and an EMPTY context compartment. What resolves it is a reply-to token that CHANGES COMPARTMENT on the way home: each asker stamps `context.recall_caller` on its own `recall` exit, the hive carries a key it never named through untouched, and the hive's own exit hands it back on `hop.recall_caller` -- so the core's door is guarded on a HOP key, which is exactly the carve-out W7-R1 (GH #286) grants a door reading a key the probe cannot carry, and the surface's door becomes the `default`, so an absent or unknown token lands where every bundle landed before. It is the arrangement this level already uses one door over: `context.tool_caller` is what tells the surface's and the core's tool results apart on their way back from ./tools. The lane SET at this boundary is unchanged -- one `recall` out, one `in_bundle` in, and no key a caller must now promote -- and what is new is that a caller can address the core with a bundle, which it never could. GH #454 moved exactly one lane in each direction and both fall out of the rule rather than out of a decision: `answer` stopped being subtracted, because the connector that consumed it inside this level is now the member's and stands outside; `turn` stopped being emitted, because the raw wire that produced it is outside too and reaches the member's screen without crossing this level at all. GH #458 adds one lane in each direction and both fall out of the same rule: `in_pack` and `pack_ack` are new on talky@4.6.0 and cogny@4.6.0, no sibling inside this level consumes either, so both cross. GH #561 is the one place where the union rule is knowingly departed from, and the departure is sanctioned (`development-rules.md` § 8b, ADR-0020): the two lanes stay DECLARED, with a connect point instead of a door, and the four pass-through edges that used to carry them are gone. The rim of a level that vouches for a corridor no longer describes all of its occupants' traffic -- deliberately. `in_pack` is still a deliberate FAN-OUT rather than a route to one occupant -- one generation is one person's agent, and the `llm` cells behind its two rims must not disagree about who that is -- which is why `pack_ack` still travels twice per pack; what changed is that both edges are drawn by the sender at the rims and not by this level at its own path. GH #464 adds a lane in each direction to BOTH occupants and neither of them crosses, for the same reason `tool_call`/`tool_result` do not: `schemas` (the tool names a caller declares it uses) is consumed by ./tools inside this level, and `in_menu` (the declarations coming back) is supplied by ./tools and never from outside. So the lane set at this boundary is unchanged and the level grows four edges instead -- the same pair, drawn once for the surface and once for the core, told apart on the way back by `context.tool_caller` exactly as a tool result is. That is the third digit: nothing a caller at this boundary can do is new. GH #529 adds that same pair a SECOND time -- surface to core and back -- and GH #530 removes the `ask_memory` errand edge. Neither touches the lane set at this boundary, for the reason #464 already gave: `schemas` is consumed by an occupant inside this level, `in_menu` is supplied by one, and an errand name is an edge CONDITION rather than an address. WHAT THE FOUR EDGES SAY, since an edge carries no `because` of its own. (1) `./talky -> ./cogny` on `schemas`: the same question asked of the OTHER answerer. A tool the composite reaches by an edge on its NAME is not the tool hive's, it is topology of the level that draws the edge, and only the side that ANSWERS it can declare it -- `consult_cogny`'s schema used to be a hand-typed seed row in the surface's brain, and #464 replaced the hand-typed menu with an asked-for one and took the row with it. Both `schemas` edges are regular and both fire for one message: the tick asks every answerer at once, and the guarded default that carries `tool` is not affected, because a `schemas` message does not match its condition. (2) `./cogny -> ./talky` on `tool_schemas`: the core's answer, landing on the surface's `in_menu` lane and stamping `context.tool_answerer` so the collector MERGES this half with the hive's instead of replacing it -- the menu write is a `$replace`. It is told apart from the core's own `schemas` REQUEST by the lane and not by a negation: asking and answering are two routes. (3)+(4) the two `./tools -> X` `tool_schemas` edges stamp the same key with the hive's name; `tool_answerer` is the mirror of the `context.tool_caller` the request already carried. And on the consult errand, which is now the only one: `context.session_id` is NOT promoted there and must not be. It is already on the errand -- `context` is persistent and `hop` is single-hop (GH #521), the surface's keeper stamped the session at the start of the turn and nothing between there and here deletes it -- while `hop.session_id` is absent from a dispatcher's tool emission, so a modifier reading it would FAIL, and a failed modifier SKIPS the edge, which would silently kill every consult. GH #562 is the same move on the memory road and subtracts nothing from the lane SET either. `recall` and `in_bundle` were the one pair this level neither produced nor consumed: an asker emitted, this rim forwarded, the container forwarded again, and only the member did anything to the message. Both entries now carry `at: ["./talky", "./cogny"]` -- the lane docks on those two occupants and NOT on this rim -- and the four pass-through edges (two `recall` exits, two `in_bundle` doors) are gone with the hop they made. The delivery is one deep edge per asker per direction, drawn by the same mutation that instantiates the generation. The reply-to token, the guarded core door and the surface default moved one level up unchanged (GH #532 keeps measuring them there), so nothing a caller at this boundary can do is new or gone -- but the DECLARATION is a different statement, which is the second digit, and it rides in the same unreleased number as #560 and #561 for the reason `docs/development-rules.md` § 4 gives. What keeps the road honest is the mandatory hop this level does NOT claim: a level that declares a lane without an `at` may not be skipped, and the member declares both of these without one.
description.contract_in: THIRTEEN lanes, and they are of two kinds. ELEVEN are at the assistant's own path: in_turn, in_advice, in_sweep, in_prune, in_round_sweep, in_build_result, in_export, in_import, in_tool and in_menu (the memory's two answers on their way back to the generation that asked, GH #552) and mutation_committed (the mutation door's receipt, GH #553, carried on into `./talky` and `./cogny`). TWO are CORRIDOR lanes that name connect points below the rim and never arrive at it (GH #559, `at`): in_bundle and in_pack, both docking on `./talky` and `./cogny`. A corridor lane owes this rim no door and is not counted where prose says "all at the assistant's own path" -- what it says instead is who may dock where, and that this level may not be skipped.
description.contract_out: TWELVE lanes, of the same two kinds. TEN leave the assistant's own path: answer, write, turn_write, extraction, prune, error, build, dump and -- since GH #552 -- tool and schemas, the memory road's outbound half. TWO are CORRIDOR lanes leaving the two occupants rather than this rim (GH #559, `at`): recall and pack_ack, both docking on `./talky` and `./cogny`. The member consumes answer, recall, extraction and dump itself; the others cross it.
